chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Bakr ibn Abu Sammak, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you stand (for prayer) at night, brush your teeth, for the angel comes to you and places his mouth upon your mouth, and there is no letter you recite and speak with except that it ascends with it to the sky, so let your mouth be of good aroma.'
ai.seo_question: Why should one brush their teeth before night prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links physical purity (taharah) with spiritual elevation, noting that angels carry every recited letter to the heavens, making fresh breath a vessel for divine connection. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the interplay between bodily cleanliness and the metaphysical reception of the Quranic word during night prayers (Salat al-Layl). The instruction underscores that even minor acts like using the siwak enhance the sanctity of one's recitation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Abu Bakr Bin Abu Sammak who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Whenever you stand (for the Salaat) at night, so brush your teeth for the Angel comes to you, so he places his mouth upon your mouth, and there is none from the letters you recite and speak with except that he ascends with it to the sky, therefore let your mouth be with good aroma’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad from abu Bakr ibn abu Sammak who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you wake up during the night (for Salah (prayer)) you should brush your teeth; the angel comes and places his mouth over your mouth. Every word you say, he climbs with it to the heaven. Your mouth should have a pleasant smell.’”
